payload.title: Google login creates duplicate user records causing session confusion
payload.body:
## Evidence
When a user registers via email (gets random hex ID) and later logs in with Google OAuth, the callback in `AuthController::callback()` calls `upsert('users', ['id' => $user['sub'], ...])` which uses Google's `sub` as the record ID. Since `upsert` looks up by `id` and the existing record has a different ID (the registration hex), a DUPLICATE user record is created.

## Affected paths
- `app/Controllers/AuthController.php:18-23` — callback method

## Fix applied
In `AuthController::callback()`, before upserting, we now detect if the user already exists by email and use that existing record's `id` instead of Google's `sub`. This prevents duplicate records and ensures the Google login reuses the same user identity.

## Acceptance
- [ ] User registered via email can log in with Google OAuth without creating duplicate records
- [ ] User logged in via Google stays logged in (session persists across page loads)
- [ ] Existing user data (role, astrologer_slug) is preserved during Google login
